intro: Three free pieces I think are worth your time this week, chosen from the Substacks I follow most closely. Each one opens on the writer's own Substack.

items.title: Accessing Stretch Text With a Whole Class Grapple
items.why: A Year 8 teacher shows how she took a mixed class, including students in reading intervention, through the Declaration of Independence using a vocabulary preview, repeated readings and partner work. A practical model for anyone wanting to bring challenging text into their subject.

items.title: No Notes: Why I’d ban "copying from the board"
items.why: Adam Boxer makes a persuasive case that students copying notes from the board learn very little. He suggests handing out the notes and spending that time on questioning and practice instead, which would make a great conversation starter with your team before planning for next year.

items.title: Transition should extend learning, not restart it
items.why: With Year 6 students about to head off to secondary school, Myatt asks secondary teachers to look closely at what students have already learned so that Year 7 builds on it rather than starting again. Her four questions would be a great focus for a transition meeting.
